result:
Fixed two bugs. A 429 with `retry-after-ms: 1500` now retries after 1.5s.

- **Retry:** `should_retry` in `anthrouter/http_util.py` had the 429 check inverted. It retried only when there was no retry guidance, so a 429 carrying `retry-after-ms` went straight to the client. It now returns `parse_retry_after(resp) is not None`.
- **Wait:** the retry loop in `anthrouter/transport.py` ignored the header and always used exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s). It now calls `retry_delay(resp, attempt)`, which uses the upstream value and falls back to backoff. I added the `retry_delay` import.

I didn't run a test of the 429 case itself.

The full suite gave 1125 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped. The failures are in `tests/test_handlers.py`, in tier-routing tests. Two of them fail the same way with my changes stashed, so they predate the fix. I only saw the names of two of the three failures (`test_cached_tier_is_not_replayed_into_a_different_requested_tier` and `test_locked_baseline_scopes_the_tier_slot_by_the_lock`) and didn't identify the third.
